r.t: The Web of 2022 is very different from (and for many, decidedly inferior to) the Web of 2002. It is not enough that we work to decrease the labor costs and increase the profit margins of Facebook and Twitter.
Hypertext and the World Wide Web were built on big ideas and understanding those ideas might help us rebuild them.

slides.title: Any Questions / Comments / Doubts / Concerns?
points: **Architectural constraints** are chosen to reach a desired **non-functional profile**: Lego, Gothic cathedrals, Bologna, Unix, networking
Every constraint induces **trade-offs**: uniform interfaces gain **interoperability** and lose **design freedom**
Which hypertext design is «better» **depends on the targeted non-functional requirements**; the Web succeeded with a simpler model than Xanadu
**REST** combines **six constraints**: client-server, statelessness, cacheability, layered system, code-on-demand (optional), uniform interface
The **uniform interface**: identifiers, manipulation via representations, self-descriptive messages, hypermedia
